idea: Specialist UK housebuilder and building products research
buyer: Generalist and sector PMs holding housebuilders
pain: Housebuilder analysis requires understanding what actually gets built and what it costs
v1: An initiation on two housebuilders with a construction-cost lens
verdict: Narrow but genuinely differentiated; the sector is small enough that client count is the constraint.

why.distribution: Direct to warm PMs, and holders of UK housebuilders are an identifiable list.
why.demand: Sector research is bought, though UK housebuilders are covered by the remaining sell side.
why.fmf: Knowing what a house actually costs to build is a genuine edge over a pure financial analyst.
why.defensibility: The construction-cost angle is hard to copy without her background.
why.tailwind: UK housebuilding is rate and planning constrained; volumes are weak.
why.ceiling: £1,200/mo x 14 funds = £202k, but the number of funds with meaningful UK housebuilder exposure is limited.

ceiling_arithmetic: £1,200/mo x 14 funds = £202k. The universe of funds with enough UK housebuilder exposure to pay £14k/yr for specialist coverage is perhaps 25-40 firms. Realistic: 5-6 = £72-86k.
carries: A defensible angle no financial analyst can replicate, sold to a warm and identifiable list.
kills: A small buyer universe in a sector currently out of favour.
test: Ask four PMs holding housebuilders what they wish they understood better.
test_pass: They name construction cost or land pipeline reality.
test_fail: They say the sell side covers it adequately.
